findings.description: `-c merge.verifySignatures=false` is only a config default: a session-planted `branch.<target>.mergeOptions=--verify-signatures` is parsed after config and re-arms verification on the gate's `merge --ff-only`, running the planted `gpg.program` outside the sandbox.
findings.body:
**`branch.<target>.mergeOptions` gets around `merge.verifySignatures=false`**

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/12aaf05b9402aefb8f66f5af16242df9ef07a107/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L621-L623>

Decision 79 says the gate's `merge --ff-only` no longer runs a planted `gpg.program`. The protection is [`-c merge.verifySignatures=false`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/12aaf05b9402aefb8f66f5af16242df9ef07a107/src/core/git-diff.client.ts#L58-L59), but that only sets a config default.

`git merge` (`builtin/merge.c`) reads options in this order:
1. config, including `-c` values;
2. `branch.<current-branch>.mergeOptions`, parsed with the same option table;
3. the command-line arguments.

So a planted `--verify-signatures` beats the `-c` pin.

How a session gets there:
- It writes `branch.main.mergeOptions=--verify-signatures` next to `gpg.program` in the shared `$GIT_COMMON_DIR/config`. [`ARMED_DRIVER_KEY`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/12aaf05b9402aefb8f66f5af16242df9ef07a107/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L281) only matches filter and merge drivers, so nothing refuses the key.
- It bases its branch on the target itself, so the `isAncestor` check at L340 skips the rebase and the forged `gpgsig` tip reaches the merge unchanged.
- The gate's merge then verifies that tip and runs the program in the main checkout. This is the exposure decision 79 sets out to close.

A `-c` can't clear this in general, because the key contains the branch name. A command-line flag is parsed last, so pass `--no-verify-signatures` explicitly.

Please also:
- say in the `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` JSDoc and in decision 79 why this one is a flag rather than a `-c`;
- add a case to `signatureArmedRepo()` with `git config branch.main.mergeOptions --verify-signatures`.

This is medium confidence: the option-order claim comes from reading git source under a static review, and the planted config was not reproduced.

findings.description: The new comment says the rebase is "the one `pup merge` always takes", but the gate skips the rebase when the branch is already based on the target (merge-gate.service.ts:340-344). Say "whenever the target has moved" to match the test name.

The control comment still says "without the two `-c` pairs, `log` and `merge` both run it". This delta added a third pair and a separate rebase control, so that wording is stale. Use "without the `-c` pairs".
The decision 79 paragraph edit leaves a short dangling line ("fires none. An operator who relies") before full-width lines. Re-wrap the paragraph to the surrounding width.

The JSDoc sentence chains "A on X, and B on Y, and a `%G?` in Z — pinned to `%s`…". The em-dash aside belongs only to the rebase item but reads as if it covers the whole list. Make the rebase item its own sentence.

process_issues.description: The conventions reviewer reported that the .claude/rules injection returned only `@docs/conventions/...` import lines, not the rule text. It did not read general.md, naming.md or testing.md directly, so its review rested on AGENTS.md, decision text and sibling-file patterns.

Skipped review-maintainability and review-context. The delta is about 37 lines: one config-constant entry, a JSDoc and decision-text edit, and two tests. It has no structural logic and touches no spec, protocol or infra surface.
